items.label: Margin of Safety vs measured share

blocks.text: The connections clearing fastest are non-firm — interruptible by contract. The market prices damage; the peril is availability.

Britain is reconnecting industry to a network that cannot promise firm power at queue speed. Data centres and grid-scale assets contract for always-on availability while the connections that clear the queue retain the operator's right to curtail. That gap — between what the asset loses and what the policy pays — is the subject of this index.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Over the past year we formalised a scoring framework for the UK insurance-market participants standing in the path of that risk: carriers, MGAs, brokers, underlying assets, and reinsurers. We measured the two things that actually matter — Exposure to non-firm, curtailable load and Preparedness to underwrite it — and reduced each entity to a single number: the Margin of Safety.

How large is the bet? We score five sub-factors: book concentration on energy and compute, non-firm intensity in the portfolio, aggregation on shared grid geography, the trigger gap between damage-BI and curtailment loss, and tenor mismatch between multi-year cover and evolving connection terms.

Can this entity actually carry the risk it has written? Data and monitoring, product fit for non-damage triggers, underwriting expertise, capital and reinsurance, and pricing models built for compound interruption loss — not property damage frequency.
Every scored entity plotted by Exposure vs Preparedness. Quadrants split at the in-sample median. Dot size = confidence; fill = measured share.{{fact:total}} entities on the current slice.

blocks.text: Entities with large positive margin but low measured share are hypotheses, not findings. The scatter below plots Margin of Safety against the share of each score grounded in registers and filings — the epistemic hygiene the publication gate enforces.

blocks.caption: Each dot is one entity. Measured share = blend-weighted deterministic input.

blocks.text: Carriers, MGAs and brokers, underlying assets, and reinsurers sit at different points in the stack — and carry different parts of the same correlated cluster.{{fact:l1}} carriers · {{fact:l2}} market participants · {{fact:l3}} assets · {{fact:l4}} reinsurers.

blocks.text: At the carrier level, exposure and preparedness diverge in ways the headline score hides. A syndicate with strong capital and weak register measurement can sit in whitespace on assessed inputs alone — until Gate 2 lands on a linked asset.
Each dot is one linked asset, positioned by its Margin of Safety. The dashed line is the carrier average. Click a dot to explore — the same drill-down the index uses for every entity.

blocks.caption: Portfolio-level margin of safety by linked asset.
Quadrant split by carrier — top entities by linked asset count.

blocks.text: The index is not the product. The index is the wedge: register-native measurement of a peril the market underwrites blind, so the cover that closes the trigger gap can be priced and placed with eyes open.

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

blocks.caption: Market responses already in force — the line forming around the gap.

blocks.text: Gate 1 and Gate 2 made firmness a register fact. CMP448 priced progression. The demand queue is measured in tens of gigawatts. Brokers have placed billion-dollar DC facilities. The rules landed before the market repriced who can carry the interruptible half.

blocks.caption: Rules in force that re-price firmness — not what is proposed.
